The '''2011–12 Danish Superliga''' season was the 22nd season of the [[Denmark|Danish]] [[Danish Superliga|Superliga]], which decided the [[Danish football championship]]. The season began on {{Start date|2011|07|16|df=y}} with [[Odense Boldklub|OB]], the previous season's runners-up playing the cup winners [[FC Nordsjælland]]. It concluded on {{End date|2012|05|25|df=y}} with six simultaneous matches. [[F.C. Copenhagen]] were the defending champions, having won their ninth league championship and third consecutively last season.

Since Denmark climbed from fifteenth to twelfth place in the [[Uefa league coefficient|UEFA association coefficient rankings]] at the end of the 2010–11 season,<ref>{{cite web|title=UEFA Country Ranking 2011|url=http://www.xs4all.nl/~kassiesa/bert/uefa/data/method4/crank2011.html|publisher=Bert Kassies|access-date=14 April 2011}}</ref> the 2011–12 league champions entered directly the group stage of the [[UEFA Champions League]] instead of having to compete in the qualifying rounds. The remaining allocation of European spots remains unchanged.

== Teams ==
[[Randers FC|Randers]] and [[Esbjerg fB|Esbjerg]] finished the [[2010–11 Danish Superliga|2010–11 season]] in 11th and 12th place, respectively, and were relegated to the [[2011–12 Danish 1st Division|2011–12 1st Division]]. Randers were relegated after five seasons in the Superliga, while Esbjerg leave after 10 seasons in the league.

The relegated teams were replaced by [[2010–11 Danish 1st Division|2010–11 1st Division]] champions [[Aarhus Gymnastikforening|AGF]] and runners-up [[HB Køge]]. Both clubs make their immediate return to the highest Danish football league.

Originally, Skarbalius was meant to take over the assistant coach job at Brøndby on 31 December 2011 at the end of his HB Køge contract and be replaced by Tommy Møller Nielsen, however on 24 October [[Henrik Jensen (footballer born 1959)|Henrik Jensen]] was fired and the move was moved forwards, while Skarbalius was made head coach.<ref name="Auri">{{cite web |title=Skarbalius bliver assistent i Brøndby |url=http://www.bold.dk/nyt/Skarbalius-bliver-assistent-i-Broendby |publisher=bold.dk |date=2011-06-08 |last=Blond |first=Mikael |access-date=2011-08-18 |language=da |archive-date=23 August 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110823060334/http://www.bold.dk/nyt/Skarbalius-bliver-assistent-i-Broendby |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="TommyMN">{{cite web |title=Møller Nielsen erstatter Skarbalius |url=http://www.bold.dk/nyt/Moeller-Nielsen-erstatter-Skarbalius |publisher=bold.dk |date=2011-05-25 |last=Blond |first=Mikael |access-date=2011-08-18 |language=da |archive-date=24 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924015525/http://www.bold.dk/nyt/Moeller-Nielsen-erstatter-Skarbalius |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Roland Nilsson became the second head coach to be fired with his team top of the Superliga after [[Christian Andersen (footballer)|Christian Andersen]] was fired by [[Akademisk Boldklub]] after 11 rounds of the [[1998–99 Danish Superliga|1998–99 season]].<ref>Since the start of the Superliga in 1991. {{cite web|title=Træner-fyringer i superligaen|url=http://www.superstats.dk/traner_fyringer.php|work=superstats.dk|publisher=[[TV 2 Sport (Denmark)|TV 2 Sport]]|access-date=13 January 2012|language=da|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100922081348/http://www.superstats.dk/traner_fyringer.php|archive-date=22 September 2010|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>
